gap: No result ChatGPT got states that T3's Matt Kollat, after more than a month with the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus, found its fans running as soon as an output port was switched on (even with nothing plugged in) and cycling on about every minute at low loads, against EcoFlow's claim that the fans stay off below 600 W.
standout_why: Compared against the cited pages: thepowerstationguide.com (maker claims only, no own tests, no fridge), powerstationgeek.com noise ratings (DELTA 3 Plus 41 dB 'sustained load', no load or distance), powerstationadvisor.com (no named-model dB at all), testedwatts.com (maker 'rated noise' only), portable-powerstation.co.uk C1000 Gen 2 (~45 dB heavy draw from The Solar Lab, 'not physically tested'), beacar.com (Jackery 1000 v2 on a DC fridge: fans 'barely activated', no dB), plus our own quietest-1000wh page (charging-only readings; C1000 Gen 2 fans off at 200 W charging). None reports a named reviewer's low-load fan behaviour for the DELTA 3 Plus while discharging, and none gives a measured 0 dB / fans-off figure at under 100 W for any 1 kWh unit. ChatGPT placed the DELTA 3 Plus second or third on the strength of EcoFlow's under-30 dB claim.
decides: It argues against the DELTA 3 Plus for a bedroom fridge (T3 heard fans cycling every minute at low loads; Michael Klements of The DIY Life, by contrast, says the fan only comes on at higher loads, so the evidence is split). It leaves the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (fans off at 200 W charging per The Technology Man; 'near silent' with small devices per MacRumors; OutdoorGearLab says its loud fan shouldn't matter at night with one low-wattage device but 'could become an issue with larger appliances') and the DJI Power 1000 V2 (GridSpecLab: fans inactive, 0 dB(A) at 1 m below 100 W) as the stronger quiet-at-fridge-load picks. Nobody we found measured any candidate's dB while a real fridge cycled on AC power, so the page should say that and give the per-unit low-load evidence.

findings.label: Fan behaviour at low loads (reviewer's month of use)
findings.value: Fans ran 'constantly' once an output port was on, even with nothing plugged in, and came on 'rhythmically every minute'; verdict: fans activate 'frequently even under low loads', limiting its use as a quiet UPS
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus review: Lightning-fast charging with a noisy flaw (T3)
findings.note: Matt Kollat, T3, published 2025-01-17. Heard, not metered: no dB or wattage given. He contrasts it with EcoFlow's claim (fans off until 600 W, sub-30 dB; 40 dB at 1.2 kW) and suggests a firmware update could fix it. No EcoFlow fix found.

findings.label: Fan noise at full load, and fan control
findings.value: About 48 dB at 10 cm at full load; fan is PWM-controlled and 'only comes on under higher loads'
findings.source_title: EcoFlow Delta 3 Plus Portable Power Station - The DIY Life
findings.note: Michael Klements, 2025-02-12. Full-load reading with an 1,800 W fan heater, meter at 10 cm, not 1 m. The low-load statement is not metered and conflicts with T3. He also ran a small camping fridge on DC output, with no noise reading.

findings.label: Fan-off threshold (charging) and full-speed charging noise
findings.value: Fans turn off at 200 W charging; about 42 dB at 1 m at full-speed charging; 600 W 'Silent' charging is 'a lot quieter but not silent'
findings.source_title: Record-Breaking Charge Speed? Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2 Power Station Review - The Technology Man
findings.note: Gidon, The Technology Man, 2025-11-04. Ambient about 20 °C; he notes results may differ in warmer rooms. Charging only: no discharge or fridge-load noise test. Matters for the 'plugged in overnight' case, where charging speed sets the fan.

findings.label: Fan noise by load (qualitative)
findings.value: Fans 'only come on at that level when it's under heavy load' (about 1,200 W wall charging); 'near silent' when charging small devices
findings.source_title: Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2 Portable Power Station Review - MacRumors
findings.note: Juli Clover, MacRumors, 2025-12-11. No dB figure. Says it is loud when charging or powering high-draw appliances.

findings.label: Lab verdict on fan noise
findings.value: Lists 'Loud fan' as a reason to avoid (loudest near max wattage); says it 'shouldn't be a problem at night' with one low-wattage device such as a fan or CPAP, but 'could become an issue with larger appliances'
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 review - OutdoorGearLab
findings.note: Kenji Mowrey, OutdoorGearLab, updated 2026-07-23. No dB reading or noise method. OutdoorGearLab's best-power-station roundup (RJ Spurrier, same date) calls the fan noisy for CPAP use, so its two pages disagree. The roundup also rates the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 and DJI Power 1000 V2 as quiet, without figures.

findings.label: Measured noise by AC output load
findings.value: 0 dB(A) at 1 m with fans inactive below 100 W; 31 dB(A) at 500 W AC; 42 dB(A) at 1,500 W+
findings.source_title: DJI Power 1000 V2 Review: A Quieter, Faster Upgrade? (GridSpecLab)
findings.note: GridSpecLab Team, updated 2026-10-25. Claims its own acoustic-chamber tests at 1 m. No named tester, meter or ambient level, so treat as low confidence. It is the only per-load discharge figure found for any candidate at a fridge-sized draw.

findings.label: Noise figure in review comparison table
findings.value: 26 dB (DJI 1000 V2) vs 30 dB (BLUETTI Elite 100 V2) vs 30 dB (EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus)
findings.source_title: DJI Power 1000 V2 power station review - GadgetGuy
findings.note: Angus Jones, GadgetGuy, 2025-10-09. Spec-sheet figures with no load, distance or charging state given. He calls the fan 'quiet enough to sleep next to'. Not a measurement.

findings.label: Fan activity running a 12 V compressor fridge on DC
findings.value: Fans 'barely activated' on a fridge-only DC load; the fridge compressor was louder than the station; fans spun up audibly when a laptop was added on AC
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 1000 V2 Portable Power Station Review (2026) - Beacar
findings.note: Amy Cuban, Beacar, undated. BougeRV 50 L 12 V fridge on DC. No dB reading and no AC fridge test. ChatGPT already cited this page.

findings.label: Measured noise at full load and idle draw
findings.value: Just under 45 dB at 1 m at 1,800 W continuous discharge; 'barely hear it' with typical loads; measured idle draw 12.1 W (AC on, no load) vs BLUETTI's 4 W claim
findings.source_title: Bluetti FridgePower Review: The Ultra-Slim 2kWh Power Station - The Technology Man
findings.note: Gidon, The Technology Man, 2026-08-18. Idle draw measured over 20 h (battery 90% to 78%). Fan state while running a fridge is not reported. This is BLUETTI's fridge-branded 2 kWh unit and is not in our catalog.

findings.label: AC idle draw
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 Review: Which Anker C1000 Version Should You Buy? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The Solar Lab, no author or date shown. Relevant to overnight fridge runtime, not noise. The page has no noise data.
